title: Word Pattern II
summary: Determine if a string matches a given pattern by establishing a one-to-one correspondence between each pattern character and a non-empty substring of the string, ensuring no two pattern characters map to the same substring.
statement: Determine if a string matches a given pattern by establishing a one-to-one correspondence between each pattern character and a non-empty substring of the string, ensuring no two pattern characters map to the same substring.
constraints: pattern and s contain 1–20 and 1–50 lowercase English letters, respectively.
Return whether every pattern character can map bijectively to one nonempty substring so concatenating the mapped substrings in pattern order equals all of s.
hints: Mappings must be consistent in both directions: character→substring and used substrings.
At an unmapped character, try each nonempty next substring that leaves at least one character per remaining pattern position.
Assign an unused candidate, recurse on both advanced indices, then remove it on failure. Reuse an existing mapping only when s starts with it.
Succeed only when both pattern and text end together; exhausting just one side is not a complete match.
editorial: Backtracking consumes the pattern and text from left to right. Existing mappings force one exact prefix. A new character tries each feasible unused substring, and the used set enforces bijection. Removing speculative assignments restores the search state. The independent oracle enumerates every way to partition short generated text into exactly len(pattern) nonempty pieces and checks the two mappings directly.

tests.explanation: Mapping a→red and b→blue expands abab to the complete text.
Both one-character splits would map a and b to the same substring a, violating the bijection.
